title: Graceful KV eviction and switchover controller for Private data-plane rollouts
creator: Anika Shah
description:
Context:
We need a controller/operator that enables zero-downtime runtime/data-plane upgrades for Private (VPC) deployments by orchestrating graceful KV/cache eviction, staged switchover, and automated rollback when health gates fail. Existing approaches (drain-heavy restarts, full tenant outages, or naive traffic cutovers) are causing customer-visible latency spikes and transient 5xxs during scheduled upgrades. This ticket is the plan & implementation epic for a controller that coordinates the following: KV-aware eviction, slot rebinds, per-tenant canaries, traffic quiesce phases, and automated rollback with root-cause capture.

Goals:
- Maintain <2% error budget burn for customers during rolling upgrades (per-tenant SLOs).
- Avoid cold-cache-induced token/regeneration spikes by performing primed eviction with background re-warm policies where possible.
- Provide deterministic, observable rollback when any of the health gates trip.
- Make the controller usable in Private (VPC) installs: IaC hooks (Terraform module outputs), operator CRDs, RBAC checks, and an upgrade-run audit log.

High-level approach and design decisions:
- Controller model: Kubernetes-style operator that watches UpgradeRequest CRD (for Private on-prem and VPC control plane) and Machine/Slot state. The operator executes a state machine: PREPARE -> PRIMED_EVICT -> CANARY -> GRADUAL_SHIFT -> VERIFY -> FINALIZE.
- Health gates: Multi-signal gating combining (1) latency p95/p99, (2) error rate (5xx/timeout), (3) KV miss ratio and re-generation rate, (4) tok/sec throughput, and (5) per-tenant tail latency for active sessions. Roll-forward only when all gates within thresholds for a configurable window (default 2m).
- KV eviction strategy: Evict KV entries in a prioritized background pass, avoiding full cache invalidation. The operator triggers eviction by slot group and maintains a rewarm job (low-priority background replicas) to pre-populate cache on new runtime nodes before routing heavy traffic.
- Traffic control: Integrate with our smart routing layer to route X% test traffic to upgraded nodes. Start with a 1% canary for 2m, increase to 5% for 10m, and then a linear ramp to 100% across slot groups. Configurable policy per customer.
- Rollback policy: If any health gate fails, immediately shift traffic back to the last healthy variant and mark the upgrade as FAILED. Capture a pre- and post-upgrade snapshot (logs, metrics diff, top traces) and link to the upgrade run. Automatic retry with backoff only after human approval.

Implementation plan and tasks (owner assignments):
- CRD + controller plumbing (Miguel): implement UpgradeRequest CRD, state machine, and leader election for HA operator. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime-operator/pull/212 (WIP).
- KV eviction library (Anika): shared library to do prioritized eviction and rewarm scheduling. Add metrics: kv_evictions/sec, kv_rewarm_hits.
- Routing hooks (Infra-Edge team): add traffic-split API to router and expose safe-shift scaffold. Dep task: RFC to router team and small API PR.
- Health gate engine (SRE & Observability): implement multi-signal rolling window checks, integrate with Console dashboards and alerts. Add synthetic checks for example prompts to detect semantic regressions.
- IaC integration (Platform): Terraform module output hooks so ops can trigger UpgradeRequests from terraform apply (for private installs). Documented in: https://confluence.redwood.ai/private-deploy/upgrade-automation

Progress and recent updates:
- 2026-03-02: Spike completed for eviction algorithm. Findings: prioritize long-tailed keys and session keys first to reduce rehydration cost. Tradeoff: longer eviction window reduces memory pressure but increases upgrade time.
- 2026-03-04: Initial CRD schema reviewed by eng-arch. Conventions accepted, need to add explicit audit annotations for compliance.
- 2026-03-06: Prototype controller started performing PREPARE->PRIMED_EVICT transitions in staging cluster. Observed reduced error spikes vs naive drain, but noticed a 10% p95 latency uplift during rewarm bursts for some workloads. Mitigation: add QoS throttling for rewarm tasks.
- 2026-03-08: First integrated canary test in private-staging with a synthetic tenant. Canary metrics collected in Grafana dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/upgrade/kv-switchover-staging (private access).
- 2026-03-09: Security review requested for controller RBAC and audit logs. Added to PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime-operator/pull/212.

Rollout plan for private customers:
1) Internal dogfood: run controller in our own VPC with non-critical tenants. Validate across regional variance and burst profiles.
2) Opt-in beta: pick 3 low-risk customers with non-real-time SLAs. Run upgrades with ops observing.
3) Production opt-in: open tooling to customers with toggle in Console. Default policy conservative (longer windows).

Rollback runbook (automated steps + operator tasks):
- Automated: On gate fail, controller pauses ramp, flips routing back to previous variant, scales down new nodes gracefully, and triggers a diag snapshot job. Email + Slack alert to oncall with run ID.
- Operator steps: Pull logs via run UI link, check top traces, identify whether KV misses or kernel scheduling regressions caused the failure. If fixable (config tweak), bump a patch and re-run canary. If not, mark upgrade = CANCELLED and schedule follow-up.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for state machine and respawn conditions.
- Integration tests: staged cluster with synthetic traffic profiles (short chat, long completion, embeddings) to validate KV rewarm effectiveness.
- Chaos tests: simulate node preemption, sudden traffic spike, and network partition to ensure we revert cleanly.
- Load validation: run a 48h soak with rolling upgrades every 6h on staging to detect slow regressions.

Open trade-offs and decisions needing PM/SRE + Security signoff:
- Default canary sizing: 1% vs 5% — smaller reduces blast radius but increases runtime. PM to decide customer expectations.
- Automatic retry policy: Should controller auto-retry N times? SRE prefers manual approval after 1 failure for safety.
- Data retention for upgrade run snapshots: Compliance asked for 90 days; customers may require longer.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Eviction-induced rewarm bursts cause transient CPU spikes. Mitigation: QoS throttle rewarm jobs and distribute rewarm over a longer window.
- Risk: Misconfigured traction policies in Private tenants cause uneven traffic distribution. Mitigation: validate Terraform module outputs and add preflight linting.

Next steps (short-term):
- Finish PR for controller core state machine and CRD (ETA 2026-03-12).
- Add eviction metrics and configure Console dashboard panels (ETA 2026-03-14).
- Run first dogfood canary across two private clusters (ETA 2026-03-16).

Acceptance criteria:
- Controller can perform a complete upgrade with canary + ramp to 100% without exceeding configured SLOs in 90% of runs in staging spin.
- Automated rollback triggers correctly on any single gate failure and retains required diagnostics.
- IaC hooks available so private customers can trigger and audit upgrades via Terraform outputs and operator logs.

Notes from review (2026-03-09):
- Eng-arch: Add explicit upgrade-run checksum to ensure we can map operator-run artifacts to Git SHA + image tag.
- Security: Ensure audit logs include user identity and Terraform run id when triggered from IaC.
- PM: Provide a short customer-facing doc explaining conservative default policy and opt-in toggles.

Follow-ups (post-MVP):
- A/B rollback policy experiments and automated regression detection by semantic evals.
- Per-tenant rollback policies and per-customer safety-net thresholds for enterprise customers.

Comments:
